text: Mount Chamberlin is a 13,169-foot-elevation (4,014-meter) summit located west of the crest of the Sierra Nevada mountain range in Tulare County, California, within Sequoia National Park. It lies 3.2 miles (5.1 km) south-southwest of Mount Whitney, 1.5 miles (2.4 km) south of Mount Hitchcock, and 3.5 miles west of Mount Corcoran. The mountain rises approximately 1,830 feet (560 meters) above Crabtree Lakes over a distance of one-half mile, demonstrating significant topographic relief. It is ranked as the 119th highest summit in California. The name of Mount Chamberlin was officially adopted in 1940 by the U.S. Board on Geographic Names to honor American geologist Thomas Chrowder Chamberlin (1843–1928). The first ascent of the summit was completed by Sierra Club member J. H. Czock, though the exact date is unknown. Established climbing routes exist on the mountain. According to the Köppen climate classification system, Mount Chamberlin has an alpine climate. Most weather fronts begin in the Pacific Ocean and move eastward toward the Sierra Nevada, where they are forced upward by the mountain peaks, resulting in precipitation—either rain or snow—due to orographic lift. Runoff from the mountain drains westward into the Kern River through Whitney and Rock Creeks.
